Falenica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Warszawa, Poland

Not demolished. Falenica's Jewish community developed from the late 19th century; by 1921, 1,108 Jews lived there, most murdered at Treblinka in August 1942. The cemetery was established around 1917, serving Falenica and neighboring Wawer and Wiązowna. Due to its proximity to developing properties, Warsaw's poviat authority ordered the cemetery closed in 1927, with the process finalized around 1937-1938 as the Jewish community that maintained it was dissolved; it was officially closed on January 18, 1938, still in good condition at the time, with a brick wall, wooden fencing, and a watchman's house. Subsequent burials were redirected to Aleksandrów. Falenica became part of Warsaw in 1951. The former caretaker's house, occupied until recent decades, was demolished in 2020.
